disagreements.issue: Removal of Local Historic Landmark Designation for Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2 (Case LD1200003)
disagreements.summary: A sharp policy debate arose over whether City Council should revoke the local historic landmark designation of Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2 to facilitate a $50 million private redevelopment based on a negotiated developer-Preservation Durham compromise, overriding the Historic Preservation Commission's unanimous denial recommendation.
disagreements.side_a_position: De-list Liberty Warehouse as a local historic landmark to enable East West Partners' $50 million mixed-use redevelopment and Preservation Durham memorialization compromise, while reforming the HPC process separately.
side_a_arguments: Adaptive reuse of the deteriorated 200,000 sq ft warehouse is economically infeasible after years of failed attempts and a 2011 roof collapse.
Preservation Durham negotiated a compromise retaining the southern brick wall, northeastern facade, signs, and old wood, and documenting tobacco auction history.
Redevelopment brings $50M investment, workforce housing, Central Park connectivity, and ~$850,000/year in city real estate and sales taxes.
Landmark designation only delays demolition by one year anyway, and waiting further will not save the building.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the de-listing application under UDO Section 3.17 criteria, keep review within public Historic Preservation Commission channels, and maintain enforcement against demolition by neglect.
side_b_arguments: Liberty Warehouse remains Durham's last surviving downtown tobacco auction house and still meets cultural and architectural landmark criteria (unanimous HPC, Planning staff, and SHPO finding).
De-listing based on a developer's redevelopment proposal rather than objective historic merit undermines the entire local landmark program.
Removing landmark status eliminates binding preservation commitments and relies on private negotiations held outside public HPC review.

Critics questioned why $500/day demolition-by-neglect fines against Greenfire were stayed and argued owners should face interest/penalties when repaying tax benefits (a point Moffitt echoed for future ordinance reform).
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 6-0 to de-list Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2; Don Moffitt requested future ordinance changes to assess interest/penalties on repaid tax credits, and Steve Schewel noted ongoing Planning staff focus groups to rebuild confidence in the HPC process.

agenda_items.title: Durham Bulls Athletic Park (DBAP) 20-Year Lease and Development Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services Director Joel Wright and Finance Director David Boyd presented a new 20-year lease (effective Jan. 1, 2014, with two 5-year renewal options) and development agreement with the Durham Bulls Baseball Club, shifting day-to-day operating costs and preventive maintenance up to $200,000/year to the club, setting $125,000 base rent plus additional rent, capping city capital improvements at $12 million ($6M deferred maintenance, $6M new improvements) with a minimum $2M club investment, and yielding over $7 million in nominal General Fund savings (~$200,000/year). Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden cited $24.1 million in 2010 visitor spending and $3.3 million projected from the 2014 AAA All-Star Game, and Council Members Don Moffitt, Steve Schewel, and Eugene Brown praised Capitol Broadcasting's partnership; Bulls President Mike Goodman thanked Council.

agenda_items.title: 2013 First Quarter Crime Summary Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez presented the Q1 2013 crime report showing Part 1 crime at a 14-year first-quarter low (down 4%, violent crime down 12%, burglaries down 15% aided by the RAP initiative) and clearance rates above FBI peer averages, while noting an increase in motor vehicle thefts (including scooters and unlocked/running cars). Council Member Steve Schewel raised concerns about 12 firearms violations by 15-year-olds and inadequate state funding for pretrial release programs, Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden inquired about youth tracking under age 16, and Mayor Bell and Council Member Eugene Brown requested breakdowns on key-left-in-car thefts and progress against copper theft.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls (Donphil Road and Hersey/Percy Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Nathan McKinney of Public Works presented assessment rolls for the Donphil Road water main and Hersey/Percy Street sewer main, recommending confirmation of both rolls except for Sasha Delago's objected property on Donphil Road, which staff recommended continuing to the June 17, 2013 meeting. No public comments were offered.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2014 Stormwater Rate Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Stormwater Director Paul Wiebke presented an ordinance increasing residential stormwater rates by $2.85 to $11.82 per year across tiers effective July 1, 2013, generating over $1 million for capital projects to meet Falls Lake and Jordan Lake Stage 1 nutrient reduction goals. Council Member Steve Schewel asked whether Durham was covering costs given lower rates than peers (Wiebke confirmed 98% billing recovery), and Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden asked about legal advertising in the Carolina Times. No public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Update on Water and Sewer Connection Charges
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley presented updated water and sewer connection fees effective July 1, 2013 to recover city installation costs for new services (misstated by the Mayor initially as Item 23). Council Member Steve Schewel confirmed that the fees cover full costs despite being lower than peer cities, and no public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Update on Water and Sewer Capital Facilities Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Greeley presented updated water and sewer capital facilities fees charged to new homes and businesses to fund treatment capacity expansion based on the financial rate model, explaining in response to Steve Schewel that fees are lower than peers like Cary due to differing utility capital needs. Schewel also questioned Public Works Director Marvin Williams on why the out-year stormwater model projected only 2.0% increases, and Williams explained major capital projects would finish in 3-4 years; no public speakers objected.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Convene Closed Session (GS 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker confirmed no public action was expected following closed session, and Council voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session for attorney-client consultation in the City Council Conference Room.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Revision to Item 13 (Dunwoody Subdivision Street Completion)
votes.notes: Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield informed Council that the motion and recommendation for Agenda Item 13 (completion of a street in the Dunwoody Subdivision) had been revised to incorporate the $6,000 increase in the city's contribution discussed at the prior work session. Council moved, seconded, and approved accepting the City Manager's priority item 5-0 without further debate.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Items: Revision to Item 11 Attachment 14 and Addition of Closed Session
votes.notes: Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: City Attorney Patrick Baker notified Council of two priority items: a revision to Attachment 14 (upset bid resolution) on Item 11 for the Durham Bulls Athletic Park lease and development agreement, and a request for a closed session at the conclusion of the meeting for attorney-client consultation under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3). Council approved the City Attorney's priority items 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 8: Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Operating Agreement Modification and Extension
votes.notes: Reflects renegotiated operating profit incentive threshold moved from $2M to $3M. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented the proposed modification and extension of the DPAC operating agreement with Durham Performing Arts LLC (Nederlander and PFM), explaining that following work-session concerns raised by Mayor Bell and Council Member Don Moffitt regarding an incentive at the $2 million operating profit level, staff renegotiated an alternate incentive threshold at $3 million. Mayor Bell, Don Moffitt, Eugene Brown, and Steve Schewel all commended the renegotiated profit split and the five-year track record of PFM and Nederlander, while Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden highlighted $43.7 million in FY 2011-12 visitor spending and $4.5 million in tax revenues (plus $3 per-ticket revenue). After Cole-McFadden spoke in favor and a final motion and second were made, Council approved the agreement 5-0, and PFM CEO Lynn Singleton thanked Council.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Durham Bulls Athletic Park (DBAP) 20-Year Lease Agreement and Development Agreement
votes.notes: Subject to statutory upset bid process (GS 160A-269) with revised Attachment 14. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: General Services Director Joel Wright and Finance Director David Boyd presented the new 20-year DBAP lease (effective January 1, 2014, with two 5-year renewal options) and development agreement with the Durham Bulls Baseball Club, noting the Bulls will assume all operating expenses, utilities, and preventive maintenance up to $200,000/year while paying $125,000 base rent plus additional rent, saving the city over $7 million nominally (~$200,000/year) while capping city capital funding at $12 million ($6 million deferred maintenance and $6 million new improvements) alongside a minimum $2 million club investment. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden cited $24.1 million in 2010 visitor spending and $3.3 million projected from the 2014 AAA All-Star Game, while Steve Schewel, Don Moffitt, and Eugene Brown praised city staff, the City Attorney's office (especially Fred Lamar), and Capitol Broadcasting's partnership. Moffitt moved the item, and Council approved it 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls (Donphil Road Water Main and Hersey/Percy Street Sewer Main)
votes.notes: Confirms rolls except for Sasha Delago's property on Donphil Road, continued to June 17, 2013. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Nathan McKinney of Public Works presented Item 19 to confirm assessment rolls for water main improvements on Donphil Road and sewer main improvements on Hersey/Percy Street. Because property owner Sasha Delago objected to the Donphil Road water main assessment, staff recommended confirming both rolls except for the Delago property and continuing the public hearing and objection for that parcel without further advertising to the June 17, 2013 meeting. With no public speakers, Council moved staff's recommendation and approved it 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Ordinance Amending FY 2014 Stormwater Rate Schedule
votes.notes: Effective July 1, 2013; generates over $1M for Falls Lake and Jordan Lake Stage 1 reduction goals. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Assistant Stormwater Director Paul Wiebke presented the proposed FY 2014 stormwater rate increase raising residential annual fees by $2.85 to $11.82 across tiers to generate slightly over $1 million for capital projects toward Falls Lake and Jordan Lake Stage 1 nutrient reduction goals. Council Member Steve Schewel asked why Durham's stormwater rates were lower than peer jurisdictions and whether costs were fully recovered; Wiebke confirmed 98% billing recovery. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden inquired about legal notice placement in the Carolina Times, and with no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and adopted the ordinance 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 22: Update on Water and Sewer Connection Charges
votes.notes: Effective July 1, 2013. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Water Management Director Don Greeley presented an update to the fee schedule for new water and sewer connection charges effective July 1, 2013 to cover city installation costs for new service connections. Council Member Steve Schewel asked why Durham's connection fees were substantially lower than peer cities and whether full costs were recovered, and Greeley affirmed the fees cover the city's costs (deferring a comparison question on Cary to the next item). With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the fee update 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 23: Update on Water and Sewer Capital Facilities Fees
votes.notes: Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Don Greeley presented updated water and sewer capital facilities fees charged to new homes and businesses to cover the cost of expanding water and wastewater treatment capacity. Responding to Council Member Steve Schewel's comparison with Cary, Greeley explained each utility's capital facilities fees reflect its specific upcoming treatment plant expansion needs under its financial rate model. Schewel also asked Public Works Director Marvin Williams about the earlier stormwater item's 2.0% out-year increase projection, which Williams attributed to completing major capital improvements in the next three to four years; with no public speakers, Council approved Item 23 by a 5-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Convene Closed Session Pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3)
votes.notes: No public action expected following closed session. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: At the close of the regular agenda, Mayor Bill Bell verified with City Attorney Patrick Baker that no action was expected to come out of closed session. Council adjourned the public meeting and voted 5-0 to enter closed session in the City Council Conference Room for attorney-client consultation under GS 143-318.11(a)(3).
